summary: 20 decisions explained in 58 steps; 58 of 58 steps match the cited code; 10 of 10 claims have a card

cards.title: Most saved outputs only gain three lines

steps.text: a typical saved output gains three lines: `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, the mark `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`, and `#endif`.
in one file the opening brace used to share a line with the class (`{ internal sealed class`).
that brace stands alone, and the new lines follow it (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`).
in its sister file one empty line appears after the brace, before `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`.

cards.verdict: The AI accepts the count: only 2 saved outputs change in other ways, and both changes are explained.

because.text: A script sorted every changed saved output. It found 2 that change by more than the new lines.
because.summary: 237 files changed: 222 snapshot, 6 template, 6 generated-output, 1 test, 1 doc, 1 logic; 220 of 222 snapshots change only by attribute and #if/#endif guard lines, 2 do not; 3 snapshot files left unchanged, 1 Resources dir(s) with no test method

cards.unsure: A count describes the change. It does not show the saved outputs are right; that is the next card.

cards.title: A small helper fix was needed

steps.text: a formatter sits inside a generic class with type rules (`anyConstraints`).
the helper wrote the opening brace with no line break after it (`anyConstraints ? "{"`).
the templates now start with a line that must begin a fresh line (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0`).
the helper adds a line break after the brace (`anyConstraints ? "{\r\n"`).

cards.verdict: The AI keeps the helper edit: without it, the generated code does not build.

cards.title: Users' own resolver mark now clashes

steps.text: the generator puts the mark on the resolver class (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
that class is the user's own; the generator only fills in the rest (`partial class <#= ResolverName.Name #>`).
the combined resolver gets the same mark (`ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`).
the user already wrote the mark on their half (`partial class GeneratedMessagePackResolver`), the class has it twice and the build stops.

cards.verdict: This breaks the build for users who already added the mark by hand, so the owner must decide.

because.text: A small app with the mark on its own resolver builds on the old code and fails on the new code.
because.summary: A user's own [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their partial resolver compiles on base (1 of 1 probe passed) and breaks on the branch (1 of 1 failed, error CS0579 duplicate attribute)

cards.unsure: We do not know how many users add this mark by hand. The class can be public, so the mark also shows in the user's own type.
cards.ask: Should the generator mark the user's own resolver class, or only the classes it fully owns?

impact.who: Users who already added [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to their own resolver class by hand, the obvious workaround before this change.
impact.effect: After upgrading, their build breaks with error CS0579 (duplicate attribute). The fix is deleting one line, but a minor update should not break a working build.

cards.title: The mark is left out where it works

steps.text: every mark is wrapped in a check for the target (`#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`).
on older targets the mark is skipped (`#endif`).
the AI's reason, in a test comment: the mark is `not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework`.

cards.verdict: The AI's reason is wrong: the mark exists on those older targets, so their users silently lose the feature.

because.text: The mark exists in both older libraries, and a sample without the check builds on all three targets.
because.summary: ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute is present in the netstandard2.0 and net472 reference assemblies, and an unguarded probe compiles for netstandard2.0, net472 and net8.0 with 0 errors and 0 warnings, so the agent's `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard is too strict: it drops the attribute on 2 targets where it exists

cards.unsure: Turning the mark on for older targets is a choice for the owner. It would also change the tests and the readme.

rows: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).
All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
